initial_requirements: A child care center needs a web-based management system that reduces administrative work and lets employees share information through a central database. Administrators should be able to register families and manage enrollment, classroom capacity, and waiting lists, while authorized staff need support for routine activities such as tracking child immunizations, processing invoices, and producing information for customers and center operations.

slots.key: Key project risks and implementation dependencies
slots.value: Families should be able to update contact information, submit or update enrollment forms, view invoices and payment history, request basic schedule or contact changes, and upload documents like immunization records or other required forms. Requests that affect enrollment status, classroom placement, billing exceptions, custody-related information, pickup authorization, attendance, payment, or other safety-sensitive changes should require staff review before becoming active. Immediate self-service actions should be limited to low-risk updates such as changing an address, phone number, email, password, or uploading a required document; basic profile edits like contact details or document uploads can be applied immediately if they don’t change care arrangements or safety-related information. Requests to change a child’s schedule, cancel enrollment, move classrooms, update authorized pickup people, or alter billing arrangements should be held for staff review. Anything involving custody, safety, immunization compliance, or fees should not go live automatically. Office staff or enrollment staff should handle child record updates, waiting list review, and routine classroom placement work, with supervisors approving exceptions and final overrides. Report generation can be available to authorized office staff and managers, but not everyone should be able to see everything. System administrators should be the only ones who can change security settings, user permissions, and other system-wide configuration. Immunization records that are incomplete, expired, or do not meet center requirements should be flagged for staff review immediately; families may upload a replacement record, but the child must remain not compliant until staff confirms the new document meets requirements, and unresolved cases should stay out of compliance and be visible to staff. If a child’s immunization record is incomplete, overdue, or missing at go-live, keep the child enrolled but clearly marked as not compliant; staff must be able to see which items are missing and follow up with the family, and the status should remain until the record is verified or updated. Temporary exceptions can be supported if the center has a policy for them, but otherwise the noncompliant flag must stay visible until resolved. Allergy alerts and restricted pickup lists must be very visible before release; staff must confirm the authorized adult and check safety notes, and incomplete or conflicting safety information must trigger a review instead of allowing release automatically.

slots.key: Invoice exception handling and audit requirements
slots.value: Exceptions and adjustments on invoices should be handled as adjustments against the invoice rather than silently changing the original charge. Disputed charges must remain visible with a status for billing review, partial payments must leave a clear remaining balance, and credits or refunds must be recorded with a reason and linked to the original invoice. All changes require an audit trail showing who made the change and why. Partial payments should be accepted if needed, with the invoice clearly staying open for the remaining balance, and failed payments should be logged and shown to staff and the payer right away. Normal recurring tuition payments should go through right away unless there’s a clear problem.

slots.key: Classroom capacity tracking and enrollment status
slots.value: Each classroom should have a defined maximum capacity stored in the system, with enrolled children automatically counted against it. Staff should be able to see the current enrolled count versus the limit and a clear full or available status. If a classroom reaches capacity, the system should block additional assignments by default. It should suggest another open room or place the child on a waiting list, and allow a manager or administrator to override only in exceptional cases, with the override logged for later review.

slots.key: Data migration scope for go-live
slots.value: At go-live, migrate active family accounts, enrolled children, classroom assignments, immunization status, outstanding invoices or balances, and current waiting list entries. Also migrate basic contact history and authorized pickup lists if possible. Older historical records and closed enrollments can be deferred until later. If core record data is mostly complete, it should go live with valid information and missing or inconsistent pieces flagged for cleanup afterward; however, records with critical issues affecting pickup authorization, active enrollment status, or unpaid balances that change billing should be held until verified. Conflicting data should not overwrite the source silently and should be deferred or marked for review.

slots.key: Training sequence and phased rollout
slots.value: Train administrators and office staff first so they can use the system for enrollment, billing, and records from day one; then train classroom staff and anyone who needs to view child or family information. Use a short parallel running period to compare outputs and catch issues before fully cutting over. Switch over only after core data is loaded, staff can complete the main workflows reliably, and the center is confident that reports, billing, and attendance information match expectations.

slots.key: Conditions for exceptional override
slots.value: If someone other than the original payer needs a reversal, it should require a reason and probably approval or at least a second review, depending on the amount. Unusual reversals, such as large amounts or payments settled for a long time, should need extra approval or manager review. Payments should be held for review if they are unusually large, made right after a dispute, or coming from an account with prior failed payments. If the payer is inactive, has overdue balances beyond a certain point, or the timing looks suspicious, the system should delay the transaction and flag it for staff review rather than accepting it automatically.
